Overview

Lahore as a Business Centre

Lahore is the capital of Punjab, Pakistan's most populous province, and one of the country's main centres of commerce and industry. The urban localities of Lahore district counted about 13.0 million people at the 2023 census, up from about 11.1 million in 2017. The provincial government, the Lahore High Court and the head offices of many Punjabi business groups are based in the city. A 2025 labour market assessment cited by the EU Agency for Asylum describes Lahore as a central economic hub leading Punjab in workforce demand, driven by manufacturing, services and trade, with strong demand for skilled workers in textiles and manufacturing and for housing-society and public infrastructure projects. Garment production, brick kilns and other labour-intensive industries ring the city.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Lahore because so much Punjabi commerce and capital passes through it. International brands and buyers need to verify textile, apparel and other suppliers and their subcontractors, and increasingly to evidence labour conditions in their supply chains. Investors and lenders need to understand family-controlled groups whose interests span manufacturing, sugar, real estate and finance. Housing societies and commercial developments raise questions about land title, approvals and the people behind developers. Provincial procurement attracts integrity reviews. Litigants and creditors need asset, witness and corporate history research for proceedings before the Lahore High Court and Punjab's lower courts, including disputes over company shareholdings and membership records.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Lahore

01

Textile and apparel supplier verification

Buyers sourcing from Lahore and central Punjab ask us to verify that suppliers exist as described, identify owners and related companies, review adverse media and litigation, and look for undisclosed subcontracting to smaller units, supporting sourcing decisions, audit follow-up and responses to labour or quality concerns.

02

Family business group diligence

Many Lahore companies belong to family groups spanning textiles, sugar, real estate and finance, sometimes with political connections. Before investment, lending or partnership, we map group entities, directors, shareholders, related parties and litigation and regulatory history, so clients understand who controls what and where exposure lies.

03

Housing scheme and developer checks

Housing societies and commercial projects around Lahore attract domestic and overseas Pakistani investment. We research developers and their principals, approval status reported in public sources, litigation and complaints, and work with counsel on land record checks, helping investors identify title and regulatory risk before they commit funds.

04

Shareholding and membership disputes

Disputes over who owns a Lahore company often turn on the register of members and transfers recorded with the SECP. We reconstruct filing histories, shareholder and director changes, related entities and court records, giving counsel a sourced chronology for rectification petitions or commercial claims before the Lahore High Court.

05

Asset research for Lahore litigation

Creditors and claimants pursuing Punjabi parties need to know what assets exist and how they are held. We research company interests, property information obtained through counsel, related entities and transfers, giving counsel a sourced picture before recovery or enforcement steps in the Lahore courts.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Lahore

Lahore High Court

The Lahore High Court has its principal seat in Lahore and is the superior court for Punjab. Beyond appeals and constitutional petitions, it hears company matters and frequently examines the actions of regulators. In 2026 it asked the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to explain how membership records are created, maintained, altered and rectified under the Companies Act 2017, in pending petitions over registers of members. Its judgments are an important source when researching Punjabi companies and their principals.

Company records and SECP oversight

Companies are registered nationally with the SECP, described on the Pakistan page. Court activity in Lahore shows the limits of the record: in 2015 the Lahore High Court directed the SECP to act against 8,444 companies that had not appointed legal advisers, and in 2026 pending petitions questioned how membership records are maintained and rectified. Registry information on Punjabi companies should therefore be tested against court records, media and other sources rather than taken at face value.

Punjab security company licensing

Private security companies in Punjab are governed by the Punjab Private Security Regulation and Control Ordinance 2002 and Rules of 2003. Companies register with the SECP, obtain a Ministry of Interior no-objection certificate and then apply to the provincial government for a three-year licence. In 2026 the Punjab Home Department also made registration of security companies and guards through the Safe City system mandatory. We have not identified a Punjab licensing regime specific to private investigators.

Land and housing society records

Property research in Lahore involves provincial revenue records for land and, for urban plots, the allotment and transfer records of development authorities and private housing societies. Records may be in Urdu, may sit with different bodies for the same area, and may not reflect informal transfers. Property research is therefore carried out with Pakistani counsel and, where needed, authorised local professionals who can obtain and interpret records lawfully.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Lahore

TDSC has no office in Lahore and handles Lahore matters from Nashville. We start by confirming with the client and its Pakistani counsel the purpose of the work, whether supplier verification, an investment, a property acquisition, procurement due diligence or litigation in the Lahore High Court, and whether parallel official inquiries exist. Research draws on SECP records, Lahore High Court and other judgments, regulatory announcements, property information obtained through counsel, and English and Urdu media. Where site visits or local enquiries are needed, we coordinate appropriately authorised local professionals and agree methods with counsel in advance. We do not seek bank, telecom or national identity records, and handle personal data within PECA and applicable rules.

TDSC has no office in Lahore. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Lahore: Frequently Asked Questions

Can TDSC verify a textile supplier in Lahore?

Yes. We check the supplier's registration, owners and directors, related companies, litigation and media coverage, and look for signs of undisclosed subcontracting. Where a site visit is needed, we coordinate appropriately authorised local professionals. Findings are sourced so sourcing, compliance and audit teams can act on them and follow up with the supplier.

Which court hears major commercial disputes in Lahore?

The Lahore High Court, with its principal seat in Lahore, is the superior court for Punjab and hears company matters, constitutional petitions and appeals. Many civil claims start in the district courts. Counsel determines the forum and procedure, and we shape research and reporting to the requirements of the chosen court.

How reliable are company records for Lahore businesses?

SECP records give registration details, directors and filed returns, but filings may be late, incomplete or disputed, and the Lahore High Court has examined how the SECP maintains and rectifies membership records. We therefore test registry information against court judgments, regulatory announcements, media and other sources before drawing conclusions about ownership or control.

Can you check a housing scheme or developer in Lahore?

Yes. We research the developer and its principals, reported approval status, litigation, complaints and media coverage, and work with Pakistani counsel on land record and title checks. Developer structures can involve several related companies and individuals, so the research focuses on identifying who controls the project and any disputes affecting it.

Are private investigators licensed in Lahore?

We have not identified a dedicated licensing statute for private investigators in Punjab. Private security companies are licensed by the provincial government under a 2002 ordinance after SECP registration and Ministry of Interior clearance. TDSC keeps local work to lawful methods agreed with counsel and does not use pretexting or seek restricted government, bank or telecom records.
